title: Ghost and Cipher
premise: Emrys Ashgrove, a crash investigator haunted by the unexplained death of her family in row twelve of Flight 4471, is approached by a stranger named Kade who claims she once saved his life — a favor she has no memory of performing. Kade pulls her into a conspiracy: the crash was engineered to silence a whistleblower carrying encrypted evidence of an arms deal brokered by officials in three governments, and the cipher key was hidden in the wreckage. As Emrys and Kade race to recover and decode it before an international summit convenes, they are hunted by an assassin codenamed Vesper who erased Emrys's memory of Kade as collateral damage. In the end, Emrys broadcasts the decrypted truth during the summit's opening session at devastating personal cost — Kade dies covering her escape — but finds a fragile new family among the survivors and whistleblowers she protected.
about_author: Juniper Sterling is a former aviation safety analyst turned novelist who writes thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside extraordinary machinery. She lives off-grid on the Atlantic coast with two rescue dogs and an unhealthy knowledge of flight recorders.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Two years after the crash, she still works investigations by day and replays the black-box audio by night, unable to sleep past 3:14 a.m. A routine debris audit turns up a component that shouldn't exist. Emotional beat: grief calcified into obsession.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Kade's POV. A stranger intercepts Emrys outside her office, repaying a debt from a night she cannot remember, and leaves her a burner phone and a warning: stop auditing Flight 4471. Emotional beat: uncanny dread — someone knows her better than she knows herself.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The component traces to a shell company tied to defense contractors attending next month's Geneva summit. When she queries the database, her access is revoked within minutes. Emotional beat: the first vertigo of realizing the system itself is compromised.

chapters.title: Kade
chapters.summary: Kade's POV. Flashback fragments reveal he was Vesper's target two years ago; Emrys unknowingly shielded him, and Vesper punished her by surgically erasing the memory. He returns to finish what she started. Emotional beat: guilt sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: The Cipher in the Wreckage
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Following Kade's map, she recovers a corrupted data module from the evidence vault — hidden inside the row-twelve seat frame. It holds half a decryption key. Emotional beat: hope arriving like an accusation; her family died guarding this.

chapters.title: Three Governments
chapters.summary: Kade's POV. He lays out the conspiracy: an illegal arms pipeline laundered through crash investigations in three countries, each official protecting the others. The whistleblower's full testimony is encrypted behind the missing key half. Emotional beat: cold clarity about the scale of the enemy.

chapters.title: Vesper
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The assassin learns Emrys has the module and receives a contract: retrieve it before the summit, leave no witnesses. We glimpse her methodical professionalism — and one flicker of hesitation regarding Emrys. Emotional beat: menace with a hairline crack.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Hiding in Kade's safehouse, she decodes partial files: passenger manifests altered, her own name flagged as 'handled.' She realizes her insomnia began the night of her memory wipe. Emotional beat: rage replacing grief — even her mourning was stolen.

chapters.title: The Whistleblower's Daughter
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Tracking the dead whistleblower's family, Emrys finds Lena, a teenage girl hiding with a second copy of the testimony. Protecting her means abandoning the safe plan. Emotional beat: found family igniting — Emrys chooses someone again.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Kade's POV. A handoff to a sympathetic journalist goes wrong; Vesper kills the journalist and takes the courier's ledger. Kade barely escapes with Lena. Emotional beat: failure and its cost, counted in other people's blood.

chapters.title: What the Black Box Never Said
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Reconstructing the final ninety seconds, Emrys discovers the cockpit fought the autopilot override — proof of remote hijacking buried in a 'pilot error' verdict. Emotional beat: vindication that tastes like ash.

chapters.title: The Summit Clock
chapters.summary: Kade's POV. With nine days until Geneva, the trio plans to decrypt the testimony using the module plus a key held in a Zurich evidence archive. Kade confesses his role in bringing Vesper into her life. Emotional beat: trust tested and, painfully, kept.

chapters.title: Zurich
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A tense archive infiltration under a maintenance contractor's badge; Emrys retrieves the key half while Kade draws security away. They escape by train as alarms rise. Emotional beat: competence as intimacy — they move like they've known each other for years.

chapters.title: Decryption
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The teenager cracks the final layer overnight. The testimony names officials in all three governments — and reveals Vesper's employer sits on the summit's organizing committee. Emotional beat: awe at the youngest member becoming indispensable.

chapters.title: Betrayal Protocol
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Her handler orders her to burn the operation, including her own extraction. Realizing she is disposable, Vesper goes off-book — not to help them, but to settle her own account. Emotional beat: the assassin's crack becomes a fault line.

chapters.title: Ghosts
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Vesper ambushes them, but instead of killing Emrys, returns her wiped memory file — the recording of the night she saved Kade, and of Vesper taking everything else. Emotional beat: memory restored whole; grief finally has its true shape.

chapters.title: The Longest Night
chapters.summary: Kade's POV. Cornered in a border-town hotel, the group survives a coordinated strike by government proxies. Kade is wounded buying their escape route. Emotional beat: terror braided with fierce tenderness — they are a family now, and families fight.

chapters.title: Geneva Gates
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Summit eve. Accreditation denied, press locked out, every legal channel sealed. The only way in is through the building's decommissioned service tunnels — mapped from Kade's old contract files. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into calm.

chapters.title: Vesper's Account
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper intercepts them in the tunnels — then turns her weapon on the arriving handler team instead, clearing the path as payment for her own erased years. She vanishes into the dark. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, rendered by its most unlikely instrument.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Climax. From the summit's media control room, Emrys streams the decrypted testimony to every delegate screen and global feed as security breaches the doors. Kade holds the corridor so she can finish — and doesn't come out. Emotional beat: triumph purchased at the highest price.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Arrests cascade across three capitals; hearings begin. Emrys testifies, sleeps badly still, but wakes now for reasons other than fear. Lena stays with her. Emotional beat: mourning that finally moves forward.

chapters.title: Cipher
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, epilogue. Months later, an unsigned postcard arrives: a single cipher string that decodes, with Lena's help, to 'Debt cleared. Sleep well.' Emrys smiles for the first time in the book. Emotional beat: quiet grace — the ghost released, the family remaining.
